offence_severity: Death or imprisonment for life and fine
physical_harm: Injuries or death caused by burning with petrol
number_of_offences: Convicted under Section 302 IPC, one offence upheld
key_evidence_accepted: The prosecution established the entire chain of circumstances which connects the accused to the crime. The accused had pre-planned the diabolical and gruesome murder in a dastardly manner. The presence of a 10-litre can with petrol, the last seen theory, and the accused's sudden disappearance from the scene are key evidence.
witness_credibility: The court accepted the credibility of PW3 (brother-in-law) and PW5 (mother-in-law) as their testimony established the accused's dictatorial personality and hot temper. The court also found the evidence of PW14 (panch witness) credible as it supported the prosecution's case.
trial_duration: The trial court convicted the appellant under Section 302 IPC and imposed penalty of death upon the appellant. The High Court dismissed the appeal and upheld the death sentence. The Supreme Court dismissed the appeal.
legal_representation: Counsel for the accused and the State in the Supreme Court not stated
investigation_status: FIR registered, charge sheet filed, trial completed

appeal_history.trial_court: Convicted under Section 302 IPC and sentenced to death
appeal_history.high_court: Dismissed the appeal and upheld the death sentence

prosecution_argument: The prosecution established the entire chain of circumstances which connects the accused to the crime. The accused had pre-planned the diabolical and gruesome murder in a dastardly manner. He did not act on any spur of the moment. He cannot be reformed and rehabilitated. Thus, the penalty of death sentence is upheld.
defence_argument: The accused submitted that he left the scene as he had received a message that his sister in Delhi who was suffering from cancer had become critical, and thus, he rushed from Mumbai to be with her. The accused also claimed that the recovery of the red bucket was a fabrication by the police and that the prosecution failed to prove motive.
legal_principle_applied: Death sentence should only be given in the rarest of rare cases. The Court has to further enquire and believe that the accused cannot be reformed or rehabilitated and shall continue with his criminal acts. A balance sheet is to be prepared in considering the imposition of death penalty of the aggravating and mitigating circumstances, and a just balance is to be struck.
precedent_relied_upon: Bachan Singh vs State of Punjab AIR 1980 SC 898; Machhi Singh and Ors. vs. State of Punjab AIR 1983 SC 957; Mohd. Mannan alias Abdul Mannan vs. State of Bihar 2011(5) SCC 317; Sudam@ Rahul Kaniram Jadhav vs. State of Maharashtra (Criminal Appeal Nos. 185-186 of 2011 decided on 4.7. 2011); Ranjeet Singh vs. State of Rajasthan (1988) 1 SCC 633; Atbir vs. Govt. of NCT Delhi AIR 2010 SC 3477; Surendra Ko/i vs. State of U.P. AIR 2011 SC 970; Suresh Chandra Bahri vs. State of Bihar AIR 1994 SC 2420; Bheru Singh vs. State of Rajasthan (1994) 2 SCC 467; Sevaka Perumal vs. State of T. N. AIR 1991 SC 1463
sentencing_rationale: The accused burnt living persons to death which is a horrible act causing excruciating pain to the victim, and this could not have been unknown to the accused. The accused did not act on any spur of the moment provocation. There was a quarrel between accused and his wife at midnight, but the accused having brought a large quantity of petrol into his residential apartment shows that he had pre-planned the diabolical and gruesome murder in a dastardly manner. Such person who instead of protecting his family kills them in such a cruel and barbaric manner cannot be reformed or rehabilitated. Balance sheet is heavily against him. Thus, all the requisites for death penalty are satisfied. Instant case belongs to the category of rarest of rare cases. Death sentence awarded to the accused is upheld.
